items.summary: Reuters reports Nvidia’s Asian suppliers and partners in South Korea and Taiwan are reassessing plans amid speculation that Chief Executive Jensen Huang could be ousted over alleged extramarital affairs. The board met on Nov 11 to decide his future, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. Suppliers said a less aggressive successor might slow capacity expansion and ecosystem investments. Analysts warn of possible slowdowns in Nvidia’s long-term direction, though some investors expect limited immediate impact since current chip designs are already in production. Shares of TSMC, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics moved slightly on the news.
items.title: Nvidia Supply Chain Braces for Leadership Change

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet's first Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bond sales drew combined orders of more than US$7 billion (S$9 billion) on Nov 12, per Reuters. The HK offering exceeded HK$32.5 billion; the Singapore one topped S$4 billion. Final coupon levels came in tighter than initial guidance as Alphabet expands its debt footprint for AI infrastructure.
items.title: Alphabet's Hong Kong and Singapore Bond Sales Draw Over $7 Billion in Orders

items.summary: A Thursday briefing newsletter explores what is known about the relationship between Jensen Huang, founder of Nvidia, and Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed. The New York Times reported that US intelligence believes Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese services to spy for Beijing, though the underlying evidence remains classified. Nvidia said her interactions were “not unusual or unexpected”, while she admitted in a letter to employees that he had been unfaithful and described himself as “deeply sorry”. Nvidia’s share price fell sharply after reports its board considered ousting him. The newsletter notes speculation about whether Alice Huang could have gained access to US AI policy through her husband, but calls it unfounded without evidence. Experts suggest the Chinese agency MSS may have used a romantic relationship as a recruitment method, though China denies any involvement.
items.title: Newsletter examines Nvidia affair and Alice Huang espionage claims

items.summary: IBM announced the IBM Quantum Nighthawk r3, a superconducting quantum processor designed to run about 10,000 quantum operations across 520 programmable qubits. The design adds 10 chip-to-chip interconnects called l-couplers as a path toward linking two chips into a 1,040-qubit system planned for 2027. IBM noted the current production Nighthawk r2 already runs about 100,000 circuits per second and cited partner speedups of up to 19x across roughly 34 billion circuits. The article flagged that chip-to-chip links average 99% state transfer fidelity, below a 99.9% target, and that the larger system remains a plan rather than shipping hardware.
items.title: IBM Unveils Nighthawk r3 Quantum Processor Design for 2027 Scaling

items.summary: MIT researchers developed a training technique that produces faster and more adaptable climate emulators, fast AI models used to simulate future climates for policy planning. Christoher Womack PhD ’26 says the method speeds production of reliable emulators so their outputs can be trusted for decisions (quantity-1588-1590). The team found traditional emulators fail on unfamiliar scenarios and that realistic training data alone underperforms, so they generate synthetic datasets requiring only one full earth system model run instead of six to eight. Noelle E. Selin says cutting months-long production time will help researchers get updated tools into use (quantity-1588-1590). The work appears in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
items.title: MIT Technique Speeds Trustworthy Climate AI Models

items.summary: Two political gatherings in Dublin this week center on Europe's approach to artificial intelligence and defense amid rising cyber threats, according to Tech Policy Press fellow Liz Carolan. The European Political Community summit convenes leaders from EU states plus the UK and Canada under the theme 'Europe – strong, secure and connected,' with discussions likely covering AI sovereignty and fallout from Ukraine's drone supply disruption after SpaceX throttled it last month. A separate Irish-hosted meeting of 27 member state leaders will address AI governance for the first time at Leaders' level.
items.title: Dublin Summit Focuses on AI and Security

items.summary: A New York Times report alleges that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair, with five sources identifying Kimberly Powell as a paramour. Betting odds from Kalshi place his chances of surviving the week at 30%. The article offers several unnamed candidates for succession, including Lisa Su, Eric Schmidt, Lip-Bu Tan, Bret Taylor, Ian Buck and Lori Huang, while noting that Nvidia has no apparent succession plan.
items.title: Speculating on Nvidia's Possible CEO Successors Amid Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: The New York Times reported that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang is suspected of a second extramarital affair, with vice president Kimberly Powell. Five employees reportedly told the outlet they saw the couple being affectionate at a San Jose hotel during an earlier conference. TechCrunch sought comment from Nvidia; its board has already investigated his admitted affair and may oust him. Two House Republicans said Congress is preparing to subpoena Huang over spy allegations.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces second affair reports and board ousting

items.summary: Databricks announced updates to its Genie Agents, which help teams turn business questions into actionable insights grounded in enterprise context. The agents now analyze unstructured documents within Unity Catalog volumes, connect to tools via native MCP connectors, and can be shared externally through OpenSharing or privately through Genie Clean Rooms. Databricks claims 80% of the context that runs an enterprise lives in documents such as contracts and reports (quantity-1901-1904). Vinodh Simon of Verana Health said his team plans to use Genie Agents for unstructured clinical data, while Slack's Jaime DeLanghe praised bringing governed insights into workflows. Unstructured analysis is in Public Preview; MCP connectors are generally available; OpenSharing and Genie Clean Rooms remain in beta.
items.title: Databricks Unveils Genie Agents Updates for Data Analysis and Sharing

items.summary: Australia's workplace relations minister Amanda Rishworth launched a best-practice guide urging employers to consult staff about how automation could affect their jobs, offering clearer plans and pathways into new roles. The government frames wider AI adoption as potentially raising wages while shortening hours, though the document also acknowledges hazards such as intrusive surveillance and intensified performance standards. Greens leader David Shoebridge criticised the approach as voluntary guidance lacking legal force, noting firms like Qantas, National Australian Bank and Canva have cut thousands of jobs amid AI rollouts. The Reserve Bank reported little current evidence of labour disruption but flagged high uncertainty about future effects.
items.title: Australian employers warned to prepare for AI's impact on workers

items.summary: The San Francisco Bay Area Air District board finalized amendments last week pushing the zero-nitrogen-oxides water-heater rule into effect in 2028, a year later than planned. The measure exempts about half of expected installations to ease affordability concerns. Sam Fishman called it an enormous victory for clean air and climate. Cost remains the main barrier: switching from gas costs around $7,100 versus roughly $3,600 for another gas model. Jetson Home expects a 50-gallon unit near $4,500 next year, while RMI estimates annual savings of $360 per household. Fifteen board members voted in favor with one abstaining after repeal and delay motions failed.
items.title: Bay Area Regulators Finalize Heat-Pump Water Heater Rules

items.summary: After Ohio voters ended Republicans' 15-year trifecta and elected Democrat Amy Acton governor, clean-energy advocates see new openings. Acton campaigned to reinstate efficiency measures and renewable standards, and her appointees could shape the Power Siting Board. But SB 52 still lets counties block most utility-scale solar and wind projects, and federal data shows U.S. solar farms average around 24% capacity versus a proposed 50% threshold in Senate Bill 294. Advocates hope for broader review of project impacts; critics warn the lame-duck session may undermine her plans before New Year's Eve.
items.title: Ohio's New Democratic Governor Opens Clean Energy Path Amid Legislative Uncertainty

items.summary: A Vermont homeowner building an addition faced a service upgrade that could cost well over $10,000 under the standard load calculation. His electrician’s method projected around 192 amps and pushed him toward 300 or 400 amp service with underground trenching. Instead he used Section 220.87, which relies on actual peak demand from utility data; his home peaked at just under 62 amps on January 20. After adding a 25 percent buffer and new loads the traditional way, there was enough capacity without an upgrade, so contractors broke ground with no electrification cost. Experts say many panels have headroom, but acceptance rests with local inspectors.
items.title: Homeowner Avoids Costly Panel Upgrade Using Demand Data

items.summary: Sungrow has launched the PowerStack 3.0, a commercial and industrial energy storage platform built around a standardized cabinet paired with interchangeable expansion docks in what it calls “scene-in-one” architecture. The system uses laminated LFP cells and a silicon carbide power conversion system rated at up to 99.2% peak efficiency, with a stated round-trip efficiency of at least 92%. Sungrow claims an AI assistant can generate site-specific designs in 30 seconds and lift operating revenue by 12%, though these figures are manufacturer projections based on internal modeling rather than field-validated results.
items.title: Sungrow Unveils Modular C&I Storage Platform PowerStack 3.0

items.summary: A report by the think tank Climate and Community Institute examines how climate-focused Democrats won recent elections while avoiding explicit mention of the Green New Deal, according to unattributed reporting. The article cites Abdul El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate victory as an example, noting his opponent Mike Rogers framed climate policy as a tax increase threat. Patrick Bigger, research director at Climate and Community Institute, describes these candidates as green economic populists connecting climate action to utility costs. Will Lawrence will represent Michigan’s 7th District, per self-reported information. The Sunrise Movement reorganized in 2018 after its 2018 protests outside Nancy Pelosi’s office. Aru Shiney-Ajay argues the strategy must integrate climate into all policy areas.
items.title: Climate progressives win midterms without naming Green New Deal

items.summary: Researchers at Karlstad University in Sweden used light beam-induced current (LBIC) phase mapping to investigate the local electrical behavior of half-cell solar modules, finding it can detect localized defects with high spatial resolution. Unlike conventional amplitude-based LBIC, this technique measures photocurrent phase shifts using an 828 nm laser modulated at 640 Hz, revealing how changes in local series resistance affect contact quality. The team tested monocrystalline bifacial cells from Lightway Solar laminated via Sticky Solar Power's method and compared maps before and after lamination.
items.title: Researchers Show LBIC Phase Mapping Detects Solar Module Interconnection Defects

items.summary: Singapore cloud firm Megaspeed said on Thursday it cooperated with US inspections and takes export control laws extremely seriously, retaining an American law firm to census its graphics processing units. CEO James Tan Yong Pong called compliance a fundamental priority. The company faces scrutiny after reports linking Nvidia chief Jensen Huang to Alice Huang, whom authorities suspect of being a Chinese spy.
items.title: Megaspeed Defends Export Compliance Amid Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: Procurement notices show Northwestern Polytechnical University in Xi'an bought two Nvidia H200 chips from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology for 874,700 yuan (US$131,200), per a notice dated Oct 21. The management school used them; another Sep 4 notice shows the cybersecurity school purchased two more for 796,000 yuan. AFP contacted NPU schools for comment.
items.title: Chinese University Bought Nvidia Chips Amid US Controls

items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick at a White House Situation Room meeting over the failure to blacklist Nvidia customer Megaspeed, accused of illegally diverting advanced US chips to China. The exchange followed the midterm elections and mounting scrutiny involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.
items.title: Bessent Presses Lutnick Over Megaspeed Chip Diversion

items.summary: Bloomberg reports Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang is in Beijing amid unproven espionage suspicions tied to Jensen Huang, per unnamed sources; China calls claims baseless. Megaspeed imported over $4.6 billion of Nvidia products since 2023 founding.
items.title: Alice Huang Beijing Report Sparks Nvidia Spy Allegations

items.summary: A study of Brazil's Bolsa Família, the world's largest cash transfer programme, finds that an unconditional payment raised women's formal employment by 7%, with gains concentrated among mothers of children aged three to six. The effect is attributed to transfers helping recipients overcome childcare constraints and send their children to school. A natural experiment created by a 2014 poverty threshold increase shows the benefit works best in poorer areas with stronger local education and health services, suggesting public goods complement cash payments.
items.title: Brazil cash transfer boosts mothers' formal work when local services improve

items.summary: Members of Nvidia’s board favor appointing CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO if founder and CEO Jensen Huang is ousted, according to people familiar with the matter. The full board has not yet decided; directors are scheduled to meet Wednesday evening. Nvidia stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading to a 52-week low.
items.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust Jensen Huang

items.summary: Five Bank of England researchers present a structural macroeconomic model showing that the inflationary impact of an energy-price shock depends on how tight the UK labour market is. When vacancies are plentiful relative to job-seekers, workers can recoup lost real income through higher wages, broadening price pressures; the same shock runs roughly twice as inflationary in a tight market than when unemployment is high (s4). Using non-linear simulations of an open-economy New Keynesian model built on Broer et al (2025) and Chan et al (2024), they find peak wage inflation about double, with the Phillips-curve slope roughly three times steeper in tight states. They note UK vacancies were unusually high during 2022 but have loosened since, so this amplification is less pronounced now; a renewed tightening would steepen the curve again (s73). The authors state these effects are invisible to linearised models and support using structural approaches with non-linear labour markets (s75).
items.title: Bank of England model ties energy shocks to labour market tightness

items.summary: The Nvidia board was moving toward removing CEO Jensen Huang over two extramarital affairs, according to The Wall Street Journal. No clear successor exists, per The New York Times. Huang apologized in a message to employees Sunday for being unfaithful. The board announced an independent investigation overseen by former acting U.S. Attorney Joon H. Kim and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz Tuesday, saying it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. China denied espionage claims against Alice Huang.
items.title: Nvidia Board Considers Removing Jensen Huang Amid Affairs and Espionage Claims

items.summary: The UK economy grew by 0.7% in the third quarter of 2026, its fastest expansion in two and a half years (quantity-23-27). The Office for National Statistics attributed growth mainly to strong services-sector activity led by IT (entity-151-181), with AI-related businesses reporting large turnover increases. Growth matched forecasts; September alone rose 0.2% (quantity-592-596) after August was revised down from 0.1% to zero, beating expectations of no growth. The services sector rose 0.9% (quantity-2321-2325), while construction fell sharply despite accounting for about 6% of activity (quantity-2524-2526). Commentators noted the UK had ceded its title as fastest-growing G7 economy to the US, and analysts offered mixed views on whether momentum would hold.
items.title: UK Economy Grows Fastest in Two and a Half Years on AI-Driven Services Surge

items.summary: The Guardian can reveal that the Argentinian government threatened Sam Moody, chief executive of Rockhopper Exploration, with criminal prosecution and imprisonment over offshore drilling at the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falkland Islands. Argentina sought an urgent suspension from Itlos, arguing Britain's agreement to drill is illegal amid a sovereignty dispute. Buenos Aires has passed domestic legislation criminalising the project and banned Navitas for 20 years. Moody said he faced personal risk preparing his tribunal statement. The UK argued Itlos lacked jurisdiction. Ellie Reeves warned suspension would have devastating consequences for islanders. A ruling is expected on 28 November.
items.title: Argentina Threatens UK Oil Firm CEO With Jail Over Falklands Drilling

items.summary: Nvidia's board of directors is meeting Wednesday to decide whether to remove co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid uncertainty over leadership, per the Wall Street Journal. The decision follows Nvidia's November 8 announcement that it launched an independent investigation into Huang, overseen by a committee assisted by outside legal counsel. No obvious successor has been identified.
items.title: Nvidia Board Considers Removing Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: Nvidia’s board of directors met on Wednesday after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had two extramarital affairs, one with Alice Huang (Huang Le), suspected of spying for the Chinese government. The Wall Street Journal broke the story; The New York Times alleged a second affair with executive Kimberly Powell and cited an affectionate video from San Jose. U.S. intelligence agencies and the FBI are investigating his relationship with Alice Huang. The board is weighing replacing him, possibly promoting CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while retaining Huang as chairman. Nvidia’s stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading, shedding $1.8 trillion in market capitalization over a month. Bloomberg reports on the deliberations.
items.title: Nvidia Board Considers Replacing Jensen Huang Amid Spy and Infidelity Revelations

items.summary: Reports suggest Nvidia’s board is meeting late Wednesday to decide the future of Chief Executive Jensen Huang amid reports of two extramarital affairs, a shift from Sunday’s confidence in his leadership. Partners and suppliers across South Korea and Taiwan are redrawing plans accordingly. A supplier executive said capacity expansion could slow if a successor proves less aggressive.
items.title: Nvidia’s Asian supply chain braces for leadership change

items.summary: Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, following reports that he had an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. On Sunday the board expressed confidence in his leadership; by late Wednesday its position hardened after The Wall Street Journal reported preparations to fire him. Nvidia’s stock slid more than 8% in after-hours trading, and it lost about $685bn (£516bn) in market value since launching an investigation into Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang. Analysts warn the market is pricing his departure as likely rather than a tail risk.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Ousting Jensen Huang Amid Stock Plunge

items.summary: On Thursday, China accused the United States of fabricating spy narratives as a pretext for imposing a technology blockade. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said the US side should stop creating such 'spy' narratives to justify restricting chip sales. The dispute follows reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, whom US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence.
items.title: China Accuses US of Fabricating Nvidia Espionage Claims Behind Tech Blockade

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang is under investigation over an alleged relationship with a Chinese spy and possible disclosure of confidential intellectual property, as Nvidia reportedly considers ousting him. Shares in Nvidia fell about 8% on the news (quantity-2163-2165). Carmem Domingues said "there's not someone who is sort of prepped and ready to go next in line." She likened a fall to Lehman Brothers, while another investor noted data centres are struggling with power grids. For Nvidia itself, she sees any disruption as temporary, given its long-built ecosystem.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang probe raises AI-stability fears

items.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, three people familiar with the matter said. They fear a scandal involving Jensen Huang could prompt Washington to tighten restrictions on their remote use of advanced processors that would close a gap in U.S. export controls.
items.title: Chinese AI Firms Seek Overseas Nvidia Chip Capacity Amid U.S. Scandal Concerns

items.summary: European and Asian tech shares fell on Thursday after reports that Nvidia’s board was weighing whether to remove CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia shares dropped more than 8% in after-hours trading, while European chip stocks including ASM International (2.9%), STMicroelectronics (2.6%) and ASML (2.5%) also declined. The report came from The Wall Street Journal; Reuters said the board met late Wednesday to decide on Huang’s removal, citing a person familiar with the matter. Analysts at Quilter Cheviot noted there is no obvious successor but that Huang may stay in a reduced role.
items.title: Nvidia board weighs ousting Jensen Huang as tech shares fall

items.summary: Reports of an espionage probe and a second alleged affair have intensified scrutiny of Nvidia's leadership. Analysts note the company has no obvious successor to Mr Huang, who founded it 33 years ago with about 60 executives reporting directly to him. Shares fell about 8 per cent after-hours, reaching 33 per cent below their early-October peak.
items.title: Nvidia Has No Successor Plan Amid Jensen Huang Pressure

items.summary: Andrea Castillo, a Mexican university student, describes how her view of Chinese products changed through firsthand experience. She says affordable prices do not mean low quality. The article presents her account as an example of real-life encounters challenging cultural stereotypes about the origin and value of goods.
items.title: Mexican Student Reassesses Views on Chinese Goods Through Direct Experience

items.summary: Xinhua reported that China held a gathering in Beijing on November 12, 2026, to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. Chinese President Xi Jinping addressed attendees, joined by Communist Party officials including Li Qiang and Zhao Leji. The event recalled how Sun led the Revolution of 1911 before dying in 1925.
items.title: China holds gathering to mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth

items.summary: Bert Hofman, former World Bank country director for China, Mongolia and Korea, discusses how regional trade and investment ties are strengthening amid global shifts. The upcoming APEC meeting in Shenzhen provides a platform where economies with competing interests can build consensus. Progress may not happen all at once but can begin through practical measures like customs procedures or shared standards.
items.title: APEC Meeting in Shenzhen Focuses on Building Regional Trust Through Cooperation

items.summary: An Israeli air strike hit Nasser hospital in southern Gaza Strip overnight, killing at least six people and injuring about 20, the Hamas-run health ministry says. A single missile struck a building housing surgical wards and intensive care units. Medical staff, patients and companions died, including surgeon Dr Rizk Abu Shaira. The health ministry condemned the attack as a flagrant violation of international laws and conventions.
items.title: Israeli Strike on Gaza Hospital Kills Six

items.summary: NPR host A Martinez interviewed Ukraine's former Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba about his proposals to close gaps in talks between Russia, Ukraine and Europe. Audio of the conversation was set to be released later that day.
items.title: Ukraine's ex foreign minister Kuleba on prospects for peace

items.summary: NPR's A Martinez spoke with former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, William Taylor about the ongoing peace talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine. Audio of the discussion was set to be available later that day.
items.title: Former U.S. Ambassador William Taylor Discusses Russia-Ukraine Talks

items.summary: As Russia intensifies attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, millions of Ukrainians endure rolling planned power cuts. In Kyiv, single parent Daryna Kulchytska copes with outages lasting up to 20 hours (quantity-1225-1233), leaving her home dark and cold. Officials warn life could become unsustainable if supply cannot be maintained for at least four hours daily. President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine retains enough generating capacity, though distribution is disrupted by damaged lines. DTEK CEO Maxim Timchenko said attacks have doubled in power and scale (quantity-...), hampering repairs to a major station destroyed by missile strikes.
items.title: Ukrainians face worsening blackouts amid Russian strikes on power grid

items.summary: A political-communication specialist analyses the stakes of Cabo Verde's upcoming presidential vote on 15 November 2026, arguing that the central question is whether institutions can function while preserving the separation between presidency and government. The African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde returned to power after winning May 2026 legislative elections, ending a decade led by the Movement for Democracy. Principal candidates José Maria Neves and Joana Rosa would keep both offices in one party or split them across rivals. Drawing on a 2019 study with Danielton Delgado and Susana Rogeiro Nina, the author notes that voters rarely use presidential ballots to punish incumbents, since elections often fall within the ruling party's post-electoral honeymoon period.
items.title: Cabo Verde presidential election and institutional balance

items.summary: Michael Lee from the Republic of Korea came to China in 2003, and more than two decades later he now calls Quanzhou in Fujian Province his home. In Jinjiang, a county-level city under Quanzhou and one of China's leading footwear manufacturing hubs, he found a world-class supply chain, constant innovation, and the opportunity to build his own business. His next big plan is to become a true local.
items.title: ROK Entrepreneur Roots His Business in China's Shoe Capital

items.summary: Spy allegations against Nvidia Corp.'s Jensen Huang are testing a yearlong trade truce between the world's top economies before their leaders meet in Shenzhen. The scandal gives Washington lawmakers ammunition to tighten semiconductor export controls as the January renewal deadline approaches, with some $500 billion in annual US-China goods and services trade at stake (quantity-2390-2402). Shares of Chinese AI firms fell on Thursday amid concerns over chip access; Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. slumped 6.8% (quantity-4079-4083) and Z.AI Co. dropped 9.1 per cent (quantity-4131-4143). Beijing's officials reject the spy narrative as a pretext for restrictions, while US diplomats warn of deepening bilateral strain.
items.title: Nvidia Spy Allegations Strain US-China Trade Truce Ahead of Xi-Trump Summit

items.summary: Investors fear that an ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could dampen the company’s willingness to bankroll the AI boom. The board met late Wednesday amid reports of two extramarital affairs involving Huang, prompting traders to sell Nvidia shares and those of customers CoreWeave and Naver while boosting rivals Broadcom and AMD. Shares in China GPU makers Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon jumped nearly 10%. Nvidia has sunk billions into funding data centres through equity investments and commitments listed at $164.5 billion. Analysts warn the stakes extend beyond revenue to leadership vision over the next decade.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Huang's Future Amid AI-Trade Jitters

items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg said he is building an artificial intelligence agent called Muse to help him be a better father, husband and friend. During an interview on the Sources podcast, Zuckerberg described using the agent to plan weekend baking sessions with his three-year-old daughter and secure mountain-climbing permits for his older daughter. He also uses it to review MMA gym footage.
items.title: Zuckerberg Uses AI Agent for Family Duties

items.summary: The RBI issued new domestic money transfer directions on November 11, 2026 (date-546-563), effective immediately. They cover cash-based remittances for people without bank accounts and set limits: Rs 10,000 per transaction with a monthly cap of Rs 25,000 per beneficiary (quantity-737-747; quantity-816-822), up to Rs 50,000 via NEFT by walk-in customers (quantity-1574-1580), and Rs 5,000 per transaction with a monthly cap of Rs 25,000 for ATM and business correspondent transfers (quantity-1937-1942; quantity-1984-1990). The rules apply to scheduled commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks (entity-3897-3923), entity-3935-3962) and authorised payment system operators (entity-4057-4116).
items.title: RBI Issues Domestic Money Transfer Rules

items.summary: The New York Times reported that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang attended an event with Megaspeed founder Alice Huang, whose association with him drew attention amid allegations she was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Between 2024 and 2026, Megaspeed acquired more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips. US and Singaporean authorities investigated her activities; Nvidia launched an independent inquiry after Jensen Huang admitted infidelity.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang under scrutiny

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is considering banning private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in more than one non-banking financial company, sources told Reuters. Holdings of 15% or less would face fewer regulatory checks. The move follows concerns that stress at a global firm could spread across its NBFC investments. Rules are still being drafted after public feedback and could be issued early next year.
items.title: RBI Considers Barring Private Equity Firms From Controlling Multiple NBFCs

items.summary: Nvidia faces mounting pressure over Jensen Huang's future as the board launches an independent investigation into allegations he was honey-trapped by a foreign intelligence operation. On November 11, The New York Times reported additional affairs before his relationship with Alice Huang, suspected to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia shares fell more than 8% in after-hours trading on that date, and Polymarket odds of Huang leaving by December 31, 2026 rose to around 88%. Names have emerged as potential successors: internal candidates Ian Buck, Colette Kress, Madison Huang, Bryan Catanzaro, Chris Malachowsky; external figures Thomas Kurian, Matt Garman, Eric Schmidt, Lip-Bu Tan and Lisa Su. Nvidia has not publicly identified a successor.
items.title: Speculation Mounts Over Nvidia CEO Succession After Probe

items.summary: Elon Musk said it would be an honor to hire Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, in a response on X to a post urging him to recruit Huang. The statement comes as Nvidia’s board meets to consider a future without its founder. Huang faces reports of multiple extramarital affairs and is at risk of being ousted.
items.title: Musk Says Hiring Nvidia's Jensen Huang Would Be an Honor

items.summary: Elon Musk said on X it would be an honour to hire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, responding to a post urging him to do so. Reports say Nvidia's board is weighing Huang's future amid allegations about his personal relationships and has launched an independent investigation led by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Nvidia shares fell more than 8 per cent in after-hours trading to USD 159.51 as the company's market value dropped over USD 450 billion since November 8.
items.title: Musk Says Hiring Nvidia's Jensen Huang Would Be An Honour Amid Leadership Crisis

items.summary: Speculation is growing over who might succeed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose future with the company remains unconfirmed as its board has not announced any decision. Bloomberg reports that Nvidia hired an external firm to identify candidates amid allegations of multiple extramarital relationships involving Huang. The New York Times reported the board met on Wednesday to discuss his position. Eight executives have entered focus, including Colette Kress and Ian Buck from Nvidia, along with leaders from Arm’s Rene Haas, AMD’s Lisa Su, Apple’s Johny Srouji, Amazon Web Services’ Matt Garman, Micron’s Sanjay Mehrotra, and Google’s Amin Vahdat. Bloomberg notes around 60 senior executives report directly to Huang, underscoring the challenge of replacement.
items.title: Nvidia Names Potential Successors Amid Jensen Huang Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: Nvidia's board is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, according to a person familiar with the situation who asked not to be identified. The board met Wednesday to discuss his future after reports of extramarital affairs and alleged ties to China.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Temporary CEO Amid Jensen Huang Succession Crisis

items.summary: Hindustan Times' morning news brief covers several stories, including Nvidia's handling of reported extramarital affairs by its chief executive. The company's board reportedly works with an outside firm to identify a successor as it prepares to meet on Wednesday (local time). Separately, Iran has set seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming talks with the United States.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces board succession amid affair reports; Iran sets Hormuz conditions

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday (November 12) that Nvidia’s board was preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang amid revelations about his extramarital affairs, including one with a Chinese spy. The company has faced pressure since its board announced an investigation into the alleged affair with Alice Huang alias Huang Le. Nvidia shares fell around 8 per cent in after-hours trading, and the firm lost around $600 billion in market value following the probe announcement. Reuters quoted Gil Luria of DA Davidson saying immediate removal could be challenging given no succession plan exists.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Removing Jensen Huang Over Affairs

items.summary: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah called for dialogue between India and Pakistan, saying meaningful engagement must begin without waiting for hostilities to end. Reacting to twin terror attacks in Kulgam and Kishtwar districts that killed two SPOs and injured three CRPF personnel within two days, he said those harbouring ambitions of taking Kashmir must abandon such notions. He also urged revival of SAARC.
items.title: Farooq Abdullah Urges India-Pakistan Talks Despite Terror Attacks

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi sent Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali and Gujarati New Year greetings to Indian Overseas Congress chief Sam Pitroda, responding to a video in which the Congress leader described PM Modi as a "Gujarati friend." The warm exchange contrasted with past tensions, including remarks during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign.
items.title: Modi Sends Diwali Greetings To Sam Pitroda After Past Feud

items.summary: Jensen Huang, chief executive and co-founder of Nvidia, admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, who has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. The scandal surfaces amid US-China chip rivalry, as sales of Nvidia’s most powerful chips to China have been restricted since 2022 – though the restrictions were somewhat relaxed last year. Trade records indicate over $3 billion in chips crossed from Singapore to China in a single year. Nvidia’s share price has fallen after disclosure, and the company is reportedly under criminal investigation, with Congress requesting Huang explain his interactions.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Threatens AI Chip Giant Amid China Ties

items.summary: Chinese diplomats arrived in Lithuania for their first direct engagement since relations stalled over Vilnius’s support for Taiwan, Bloomberg reported. Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said he does not expect a major breakthrough and described the meeting as one of many stages in diplomatic talks. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius added that discussions “will reveal the substance” of each side.
items.title: Chinese Diplomats Visit Lithuania in First Bid to Restore Ties

items.summary: Helle Lyng Svendsen of Dagsavisen alleged that the Indian embassy in Oslo stopped her from travelling to Hyderabad for the Bharat Summit and cancelled her visa 10 minutes before she left. She said she had political clearance, a visa and was due to speak on press freedom at the Congress-led event. Quoting ‘orders from above’ in the Ministry of Home Affairs, she alleged it felt politically motivated, possibly linked to questioning Narendra Modi in May 2026. The home ministry, external affairs ministry and embassy have not commented.
items.title: Norwegian Journalist Alleges India Cancelled Her Visa
